_doc.purpose: Single source of truth for the map feature taxonomy. Drives tile generation (osm_tile_processor classifies OSM tags through this) AND the web app (filters/rotor/labels read it). SVG class = '<category> <category>-<subtype>'.

matchDSL.a feature is: { id, category, match, geometry, label, ui, status, and ONE of subtype | subtypeFrom }
matchDSL.match: an object = AND of conditions; an array of objects = OR of rules. First matching feature (in list order) wins, so put specific/priority features before general ones.

conditions.key: {\">\": 8}: numeric compare (>, >=, <, <=); leading number is parsed from values like "8%", "0.9", "3 cm"

matchDSL.subtypeFrom: use the raw value of this tag as the subtype
matchDSL.geometry: subset of [node, way, area] this feature can match (default: all)
matchDSL.status: implemented (generator collects it today) | planned (UI offers it; not collected yet)

_doc.note: Full manifest (Phase 2b step 2). Covers all 164 web-app classMap filter ids plus the generator's structural wildcard entries (building=*, the highway road set, water/waterway, vegetation, landuse, park) appended last so specific POIs win over generic base-map fills. The web app's classMap maps each filter id to an SVG class; this manifest produces those classes from OSM tags. Some web-app classMap selectors use a SHORT class token (e.g. '.restaurant', '.bank', '.museum') that differs from the engine's '<category> <category>-<subtype>' output (e.g. 'amenity amenity-restaurant'); the web app already carries both the short alias and the canonical class on rendered elements. Each feature id below equals the web-app filter id verbatim so the two stay in lockstep.

_layers: Each category has a layer: 'base' (renders the feature's geometry — buildings, roads, land), 'poi' (a point/place of interest), or 'accessibility' (an attribute that overlays onto a base feature). A feature renders its base match as geometry and carries every poi/accessibility match as a filterable overlay, so e.g. a footway keeps its line AND is filterable by 'steep incline' + 'tactile paving'.
_terrain_note: The 'terrain' category is an accessibility OVERLAY (highlight + rotor, never hides the base path) like the others, but is deliberately ABSENT from the search index's POI category set (build-tiles.py _SEARCH_POI_CATS). Surface/smoothness/width/incline/lit are way-attributes that ride on tens of thousands of roads; they belong on the map as filters, not as named search results. Node POIs (kerbs, crossings, steps) stay in facility/mobility so they remain findable.

features._comment: A bridge STRUCTURE is man_made=bridge. `bridge=yes` is just an ATTRIBUTE on a road/rail (the road IS the feature, on a bridge) — matching it here mis-classified every road bridge (incl. the elevated Gardiner) as a 'bridge structure', so it never went through the road pass that adds the hit-corridor and lost its road identity/tooltip. Match only the real structure.
features.label: Bridges

features._comment: Streetcar / tram stops (railway=tram_stop) were not matched, so the surface streetcar stops were invisible (Bob, Union loop). The generator routes these to the flat rail-transit overlay.
features.label: Streetcar stops

features._comment: Subway / rail STATION markers (railway=station, station=subway/light_rail). Only AIRPORT stations were matched before, so Union and the subway stations had no station POI. Placed AFTER airport rules wouldn't help (this runs first) — airport stations still get the more specific airport label via their own rule order; here we catch the general case.
features.label: Stations

features._comment: Non-PATH underground pedestrian connections (station underpasses, ped tunnels). An ANNOTATION overlay on the footway (base stays road) so it shows by default + has its own hide/show filter; the dotted style is in main.css. The match is the underground-pedestrian condition; the generator STRIPS this class from PATH features (plane != surface), since the PATH is its own plane, not an underpass.
features.label: Underpasses

features._comment: Underground car parking — its OWN base category (so it can be HIDDEN by default + toggled, unlike surface parking which shows). Vehicle infra: ui.default='off' keeps it out of the pedestrian default view. Must precede parking-generic so an underground lot wins this base over the generic one. Distinct dotted-fill style in main.css (.ugparking).
features.label: Underground parking
